newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends unchanged on central bank defence.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends unchanged on central bank defence.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed unchanged against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday following active intervention by the central bank to pull the local currency out of a speculation-induced fall, dealers said.

The local unit, beset by non-delivery forward speculation and the greenback's strength overseas, fell to an intra-session low of T$27.967 before rebounding in the last minutes to close flat at T$27.939.
The T$27.939 finish on Wednesday and Thursday were the Taiwan dollar's lowest level since it finished at T$28.03 on January 7, 1989.

Turnover through dealers was heavy at US$349.50 million -- US$83 million of which came in the session's last 15 minutes during which intervention from the central bank was the most pronounced, dealers said.
"The central bank did not want to see speculators earn a profit, so it purposely brought the Taiwan dollar to an even close," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The Taiwan dollar has been under heavy attack from overseas speculators in the wake of recent tumbles by the Philippine peso and Thai baht.

But dealers say unlike the Thailand and Philippine central banks, Taiwan's central bank has an imposing warchest in its US$90 billion foreign exchange reserves to ward off speculative pressure on its domestic currency.
"The central bank likely will allow a gradual depreciation to stimulate exports, but it is not going to sanction a tumble," said another dealer.
A T$27.92-96 range was seen for Friday.
